claim: The 19 November 2026 instructions say a centre must not deliberately declare a worker unfit to make him test again, must not make or use fake reports, must charge nothing above Tk 8,000 and nothing in the name of MiGRAMS, and must report each day's tests online to the Ministry with each worker's name, passport number and visa number.
target_section: Step 2: Medical check in Bangladesh (Bio-Medical), once your VDR is approved
why_new: New: bans the 'unfit, pay to retest' trick for Malaysia and shows the centre records the passport and visa numbers.

claim: Under the 19 November 2026 instructions, if a worker declared fit in Bangladesh is found unfit in Malaysia before being employed, the medical centre must bear all the worker's related costs, including sending him home.
target_section: Step 2: Medical check in Bangladesh (Bio-Medical), once your VDR is approved
why_new: New: who pays if FOMEMA fails a worker the Dhaka centre passed; the guide (After you arrive; Step 1 item 5 'After you land') says the employer sends him home and the worker keeps the debt.

claim: The 19 November 2026 instructions require every approved centre to put up a large, visible billboard at its entrance, and say a centre that breaks the conditions faces forfeiture of its security deposit and cancellation of its licence, with a Ministry monitoring team overseeing them.
target_section: Step 2: Medical check in Bangladesh (Bio-Medical), once your VDR is approved
why_new: New: a visible sign a worker can check at the door; the article does not say what the billboard must show.

claim: Bangladeshi diplomats told Prothom Alo in June 2026 that at least 11,000 Bangladeshi students were studying in Malaysia, the second-largest group of foreign students after the Chinese (about 62,000).

claim: At the Chief Adviser's meeting with Bangladeshis in Kuala Lumpur on 12 August 2025, the problems discussed included more staff at the mission, a 'graduate plus' visa for Bangladeshi students, and regularising those who had become irregular.
why_new: Shows Bangladeshi students lacked a post-study visa in August 2025 and regularisation was unresolved; consistent with guide.

claim: Lal Mia, 54, of Chhoto Amian village, Shalikha, Magura, said he paid a broker Tk 2.5 lakh in 2006 and Tk 3 lakh in 2010 to go to Malaysia, never went and never got the money back; across four attempts from 2002 to 2012 (also Saudi Arabia and Dubai) he paid about Tk 10.5 lakh, selling four bighas of farmland and his 12.5-decimal homestead, and in June 2026 lived in a house on someone else's land, selling eggs by bicycle.
placement: Step 1: Find a real job > If an agency or broker takes your money (case)
why_new: An older case (2006, 2010) of repeated loss to brokers; the guide's cases are 2022-26. Low priority.

claim: Malaysia's Human Resources Minister Ramanan Ramakrishnan proposed a new system called 'Turap' to stop the exploitation of Bangladeshi workers at village level; Turap is also built by Bestinet, and some stakeholders in Bangladesh and Malaysia suspect it is another way to keep recruitment concentrated in a few firms, Prothom Alo reported from The Edge on 16 June 2026.
why_new: The guide says only that TURAP was approved by Malaysia's Cabinet in April 2026 and has not launched; that Bestinet built it and the concentration concern are new.

claim: About 35 Aerofoam workers who entered Malaysia legally had no valid work permit (PLKS) in June 2026 because the company did not renew it on time, leaving them in fear of arrest or fines; their written complaint to the Labour Department (Jabatan Tenaga Kerja, JTK) asked that the 35 workers' visas and permits be regularised quickly.
placement: How long you can stay and renewing (case for the Need to know on unrenewed passes)
why_new: Partly answers the guide's Need to know 'Does the Labour Department take a complaint about a pass that isn't renewed?': workers did file one with JTK; the outcome is not reported.
